name: p2-opentitan-uart-serial-peer-8o1-f1f5
description: The same OpenTitan UART target with an odd-parity serial peer: the host clocks an 11-bit 8o1 frame (start, 8 data, odd parity, stop) onto rx and decodes the device's own 8o1 transmission on tx.
notes: the RX half of the run is the FIFO_STATUS read with a stimulus byte: the host drives a complete frame with the CPU clock parked, so the device already holds the byte when the CPU reads its status word (RXLVL is bits 23:16 of FIFO_STATUS at 0x24) and then its data register (RDATA at 0x18). The TX half is the F5 case: the firmware writes WDATA at 0x1c, the device serializes it, the host decodes the byte from the tx pin and the device's own tx_done output is delivered, taken and W1C-cleared
the UART profile's own MMIO endpoint is tl-ul/1 with integrity required, so the target is a TL-UL target behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter; no APB3 target is in this build
no DMA is declared, so F6 is refused by name as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:TL-UL
this file declares the scenario; it is not evidence. The run under runs/p2-pins-serial-20261103/ is the evidence

the serial peer is declared in configs/behaviors/opentitan_uart_serial_peer_8o1_f5.json: the same rx/tx/tx_en roles and idle_level 1, bit_ticks 32, but frame 8o1 and CTRL=0x800000c3 (TX+RX+odd parity at NCO=0x8000)
an 8o1 frame is eleven bit times, so the peer holds the wire 11*32 = 352 ticks and the case line's serial_rx_bits/serial_rx_held_ticks state that instead of the 8n1 ten
the received byte is only in RDATA if the device's parity check passed: rx_parity_err would drop it, which makes the RDATA read the witness for the parity bit the host drove
